content:
Update, 4:29 p.m. ET: Apple has provided more information to 9to5Mac, included in the original post below.

San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu has sent cease-and-desist letters to Apple and Google, demanding the companies remove several "nudify" apps from their app stores. Here are the details.

App Store still struggling with nudify apps

Apple and Google are once again under fire for the circulation of "nudify" or "undressing" apps on the App Store and Play Store, as reported by Wired.

The report explains:

Chiu's letter reportedly states that Apple and Google have been "profiting from harmful technology," and the City Attorney told Wired that the two companies have "likely made millions of dollars in fees from apps that offer undressing capabilities."

The report explains:

Wired noted that, to avoid directing more users to these apps, the report does not name them. Wired also mentioned that, while a Google spokesperson claimed the company would take action against apps reported for violating its policies, Apple did not respond before publication.

This news comes roughly six months after the Tech Transparency Project (TTP) published a report exposing dozens of nudify apps on the App Store, and a follow-up investigation in April found that Apple's own search suggestions and ads had steered users toward these apps.

At the time, Apple also told 9to5Mac that nudify apps violate its App Review Guidelines, and that it actively rejects and removes such apps, including those flagged through user reporting tools such as reportaproblem.apple.com.

For Wired's full report, click here.

Update, 4:29 p.m. ET: Apple, in a statement to 9to5Mac, said:

The company also said its App Review Guidelines prohibit nudify apps, as well as pornographic or overtly sexual content, and that this applies to all developers. Apple added that developers are responsible for and must have methods to filter inappropriate user-generated content, or risk having their apps removed from the App Store.

Apple also said it actively rejects undressing apps, and that users can report apps that violate its rules, are illegal, offensive, or fraudulent through reportaproblem.apple.com.
